doc.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018

title: Lew Soloff on Lipsius as creative arranger
summary: Rowe reads Lew Soloff's view of Lipsius as the prime creative arranger in Blood, Sweat & Tears.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: That’s a great story. And actually I wanted to read, I was able to do an interview with Lew Soloff a number of years ago. And here’s what he said, partly —

Lew said, “I’m saying the real creative force in that band was a particular arranger named Lipsius. Halligan also, but Lipsius was the prime creative arranger in the band. And he’s kind of a shy, laid back sort, and he would bring in this chart or that chart.” And he really loved your writing. And he finished by saying, “Instead of saying okay we’ll do this, okay we’ll record this, it was like some members would say, ‘man that’s no good, no, no good.’ And he finally stopped.” That was his take on you.
He said you finally stopped because the people in the band that were not supportive of your arranging I guess, or something like that.
